messages.subject: What makes a searcher fundable? Harder to answer than we thought.
messages.text_excerpt:
----------
Episode 46 of The Intentional Owner is out today, and this one has two halves that both deserve your time.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1960d932-6dfa-4aee-97c6-55d37cec7ead/TIO-_46-Thumbnail.jpg?t=1788376022)
Follow image link: (https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus)
Caption: Episode 46 is live. Click to watch on YouTube.

In the first, Kaustubh ([X/Twitter](https://x.com/guessworkinvest)) and I went through a list of green and red flags in searchers that Grant Hensel ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/granthensel/)) put out.

🚩 Red flags were easy 🚩

Everyone can spot the searcher who decides to do the deal first and builds the underwriting to protect that decision second.

✅ Green flags were the surprise ✅

The qualities that predict whether someone will succeed as an owner are harder to name than either of us assumed, and we spent a good stretch trying.

A few places we landed:

* AI-built decks and models are a red flag, not because AI is bad, but because building the deck is how you learn the business. Skip that and you skip the diligence.

* Weak accounting is forgivable. Not noticing a problem is not. If days sales outstanding are climbing and you can't explain why, come to your investors with a hypothesis. That’s what resources are for.

* Investors want to see a searcher walk in eyes wide open. The risks slide is my favorite slide in any deck, and it’s obvious when the risks are set up as layups.

* Solving for maximum ownership by loading up on leverage is the short-term win that turns into a long-term problem.

In the second half, Kaustubh gives an update on [Blooma](https://www.bloomatree.com/). Revenue’s doubled, the leadership layer is the strongest it’s ever been, and the overhead to get there showed up in step functions before the profit did. We talk through what that bought him, what it cost, how he's managing cash flow with leverage, and whether a refinance is on the table.

If you own a business and are building the team that lets it run without you, listen to the back half twice.

**Jump to:**

* [[10:01] Assessing searchers: green and red flags →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=601)

* [[16:42] AI-generated materials and underwriting →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=1002)

* [[22:26] Backing into decisions you've already made →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=1346)

* [[25:09] Blooma update: operational maturity →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=1509)

* [[37:07] Step functions in scaling overhead →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=2227)

* [[45:02] Considering a refinance →](https://youtu.be/d4HKF1JYrus?t=2702)

----------———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

----------
### **LIVE—Denver**
**First-round applications close September 11**

If you listened to the first half and started grading yourself, that's the point. Every quality we discussed is learnable, and October 21 to 23 in Denver is where we teach it. Adam Markley ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adammarkley/)) co-hosts.

We’re currently reviewing first-round applications. Applications stay open until October 7, but we cap attendance and can’t guarantee capacity. 34 days out.

**Apply to LIVE—Denver** (https://rja55xy9n89.typeform.com/to/RMyCgmBN)

--------------------
Talk soon,
Sam

----------

and well-positioned for a buyer to take it to the next level. He is ready to

Detailed Description.   This 8-year-old Amazon FBA brand is a proven winner in a

category that most sellers can't easily enter. The flagship product has built

601 reviews and a 4.7-star rating over eight years, earning it a dual role as a

newborn essential and a go-to baby shower gift. That longevity has given the

account natural standing in the hard-to-enter baby category, a moat that new

entrants cannot buy or replicate.

Trailing-12-month revenue of $144,550 and SDE of $25,024 mark a step down from

2025, but the cause is the owner, not the business. Three documented stockouts,

driven by reduced owner attention and cash flow, forced pullbacks in advertising

and a reduction in top-line revenue. Gross margins held at 80% throughout, proof

that the supplier and product remained a constant.

More than $16,000 (wholesale) in landed inventory is checked in and ready to

sell, removing any near-term restocking risk for a new owner. Re-optimizing PPC

and maintaining stock are low-cost fixes. A second toy product (not included in

top-line sales or bottom-line expenses) has measurable sales and inventory

already landed, and can be expanded quickly. Beyond that, an unactivated

Canadian marketplace, where competitors already move 200 to 300 units monthly,

plus untested TikTok and influencer channels for a highly giftable and visual

product, offer clear expansion paths. Workload consists of 4 to 5 hours weekly,

outside of holiday peaks.

A proven product at a depressed price is a buy-low opportunity, whether for an

Amazon newcomer wanting a turnkey entry or a savvy PPC operator who can restore

momentum fast.

Proven Customer Trust at Scale   The product carries more than 600 reviews and a

4.7-star rating, a trust signal in the hard-to-enter baby category.

Amazon-Ready Brand Infrastructure   Brand Registry and A+ Content are already in

place, giving a buyer immediate access to enhanced listing tools and brand

protection from day one.

Untapped Growth for a Giftable Product   Canada is open but unactivated, where

named competitors already move 200 to 300 units per month. TikTok, influencer

marketing, and Walmart remain completely untested.

80% Margins with an Efficient Supply Chain   Gross margins have held at 80%,

supported by manufacturing relationships running years deep. Placing larger

batch orders presents a clear, low-risk opportunity to push margins even higher.

Low Workload   The operation requires just 4–5 hours per week in the off season,

rising to 10–15 hours only during the holiday peak.

Eight-Year Clean Track Record   The account has operated without a single policy

violation and without ever drop-shipping, a track record that can shield a buyer

from account risk.

Photogenic Product Built for Social Discovery   A new owner who is focused on

short-form video and creator partnerships has clear upside to drive traffic

beyond Amazon PPC, channels this account has not yet tapped into on the social

media side.

Landed Inventory Ensures Continuity   Existing inventory is already landed and

ready to sell, so the new owner can keep products live on day one, with no

restocking gap or interruption in sales.

Detailed Description.   This business is one of the longest-running digital

asset libraries on the internet. With over 20 years of history and a collection

of more than 20 million images, illustrations, animations, and vectors, the site

offers subscribers unlimited access for a flat annual fee, generating

predictable recurring revenue.

What sets the business apart from competitors is its entrenched position in the

K–12 education market. A dedicated school-safe version is whitelisted on school

and library firewalls, integrated with single-sign-on tools common for

educational institutions, and carries approved vendor status on school software

lists. Approximately 30% of revenue comes from multi-seat accounts, primarily

from schools, libraries, and districts.

A buyer has the opportunity to acquire a premium domain (among other assets)

with institutional credibility, though the business has been neglected for the

past few years. The subscriber base has declined due to underinvestment, and the

site currently receives substantial search traffic that is not being effectively

converted into paying customers.

The most immediate growth opportunity is to improve the sign-up flow and

conversion rate, which should capture more paying customers without spending

more on acquisition. Beyond that, a focused push into district-level licensing,

a revamped SEO strategy that leverages the site's existing domain authority,

paid advertising (which has never been attempted), and AI-assisted collection

expansion all represent untapped potential.

The sellers spend about 6 hours per week on the business and have shifted their

focus to other ventures. Most day-to-day operations are handled by two

experienced contractors, leaving plenty of time for a new owner to focus on

growth. If you have experience in EdTech, digital marketing, or managing online

communities, this business offers a recognized brand with real competitive moats

that has been waiting for someone to give it the attention it deserves.

Brand Legacy of Over 20 Years   Strong brand recognition and trust among

educators, small businesses, and creative professionals stem from the business’s

legacy of more than two decades.

Massive Content Library   The content library includes over 20 million images,

illustrations, animations, and vectors spanning virtually every category, plus

IP rights to approximately 35,000 original assets.

Recurring Revenue   Annual subscriptions deliver predictable, recurring revenue

with strong retention among loyal, long-term users.

Zero Paid Marketing   The sellers have never invested in paid advertising,

leaving an entirely unexplored channel for a buyer with digital marketing

experience.

Quick Transition   All recurring technical tasks are documented, and a new owner

with experience managing web properties could be fully operational in less than
